after: Abstract: An adaptive multiscale weighting method is proposed for multivariate network traffic forecasting to address the coexistence of high-frequency burst fluctuations and long-term evolution in hourly origin-destination (OD) traffic series of backbone networks, as well as parameter redundancy and noise-sensitive static fusion in conventional multiscale models. Non-overlapping temporal aggregation constructs multiresolution inputs, and three independently parameterized decomposition linear models (DLinear) extract trend and residual components at each scale. A lightweight window router with only 131 parameters then extracts four time-domain statistics from each historical window to generate sample-specific multiscale fusion weights. Repeated experiments on the Abilene and GÉANT backbone-network datasets show that, for 24-hour forecasting, the proposed method achieves mean relative reductions in mean squared error (MSE) of 25.77% and 43.74%, respectively, using only 8,339 parameters, equivalent to 6.41% and 2.17% of the respective LightTS parameter counts. Compared with single-scale DLinear and static multiscale fusion strategies, the maximum MSE reduction reaches 4.97%. In addition, the average underestimation error at high-demand peak points on Abilene decreases by 16.07% relative to DLinear. For 168-hour forecasting on GÉANT, MSE and mean absolute error (MAE) decrease substantially by 23.16% and 11.16%, respectively, relative to DLinear. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-complexity balance and robust forecasting performance for engineering applications, providing reliable support for backbone-network capacity planning and resource scheduling.
